task: Prevent loss or excess of quantities when creating dispatch splits
specApproval: not obtained (autonomous run); user explicitly authorized the checking fix
acceptance: An 8432 SQFT source split into 1860 and 2356 is rejected with the 4216 SQFT shortage, without removing the source, saving a plan, or inserting split records.
An 8432 SQFT source split into 1860 and 6572 succeeds; excess allocation is rejected.
Validate each source line independently even when SKUs repeat or different lines' shortages and excesses cancel.
Reject negative, non-finite, missing, duplicate, unknown, or mismatched item/unit identities at the server boundary.
The split dialog updates its balance warning and confirmation availability as inputs change; confirmation also rechecks the quantities.
Both legacy snapshot saves and v2 commands reject invalid SO/TO split changes under the existing fleet transaction lock.
Use authoritative source lines and retained active sibling definitions rather than trusting client totals or supplied source quantities.
Unchanged existing split definitions and historical records remain usable; already validated unfinished re-splits continue to work.
Decimal quantities within the existing six-decimal precision, mixed packing units, balanced multi-line splits, and completed sibling history remain supported.
A rejected request must leave plan revision, snapshots, split definitions, and audit/command receipts unchanged.
Quantity mismatches return HTTP 409 and must not be archived as successful recovery drafts; normal recovery behavior remains supported.
Transfer lines lacking a NetSuite line key use their stable local line row identity.

failureModel.browserBypass: server integration and HTTP tests for both save paths
failureModel.partialWrite: compare persistent state before and after rejected requests
failureModel.staleSourceOrConcurrentChange: authoritative database quantities plus existing fleet lock; concurrency test
failureModel.offsettingLineErrors: per-line unit, property, and adversarial tests
failureModel.falseRejection: balanced properties, decimals, packing-unit and historical/re-split regressions
failureModel.unrelatedDeploymentChanges: capture running source, patch only scoped files, verify runtime hashes and preserved configuration

setup.dependencies: No new dependencies; use existing Node test runner, fast-check, Playwright, c8, ESLint, and TypeScript.
setup.tests: Repository isolated Compose configuration, mbbs-tests.slice, bounded memory/CPU/PIDs/tmpfs; register finally teardown before startup.
setup.git: Preserve existing workspace changes. No repository-wide reset or commit.
setup.artifacts: Store specification, source capture, regression logs, coverage, mutation evidence, and deployment rollback files in existing repository artifact/tool folders.
setup.deployment: Publish the verified scoped fix to the live application, preserving production data and service configuration.
